findings.title: Group enumeration uses resource ID instead of group ID
findings.body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the code iterates resources of type Groups and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). But resources are created with name equal to the group ID (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() used as resource name), so lookup by name requires groupResource.getName(), not getId(). Using the internal authz resource UUID means findByName fails, falls back to the all-groups resource, and the returned set contains resource UUIDs instead of group IDs. Callers in UsersResource.getUsersCount and searchForUser pass this set as group IDs to UserModel.GROUPS / getUsersCount, so per-group member visibility is broken and can incorrectly grant or deny access.

findings.title: canManage() grants manage rights on view-only permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, i.e. a caller with only the VIEW scope on all-groups is treated as able to manage groups. Manage operations (addTopLevelGroup, updateGroup, deleteGroup, addChild, role mapping) call requireManage(), so a view-only fine-grained admin can create/update/delete groups. The global manage check should require only the MANAGE scope, matching UserPermissions.canManage and GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(GroupModel).

findings.title: Missing null-check for all-groups resource causes NPE
findings.body: In hasPermission(String groupId, ...) when no per-group resource is found the code loads the type resource via getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without checking for null. If the schema was never initialized or admin-permissions are disabled, getResourceTypeResource returns null and findByResource dereferences null. The UserPermissionsV2 equivalent has the same pattern but here it is reachable from canView/canManage/list paths for every admin without permissions.

findings.title: getResourceName only resolves Users, not Groups
findings.body: getResourceName handles USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE specially (mapping All users or username) but has no branch for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE or CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, falling through to resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources are created with name equal to group ID and no display name, so admin UI for group permissions will show IDs or null instead of group names/paths, unlike the user case.
